# tritonctl sandbox network

The network policy of a sandbox

Subcommands: show, replace

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox network [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl sandbox network show

Show the policy in force

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox network show [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl sandbox network replace

Replace the whole policy. A list not given is cleared, so this asks first; `-y` answers yes

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox network replace [OPTIONS] <SANDBOX>`

- `<SANDBOX>`: Sandbox name, uuid, or prefix
- `--allow-out <CIDR>`: A destination the sandbox may reach, as a CIDR block or an address. Repeatable. Allow beats deny
- `--deny-out <CIDR>`: A destination the sandbox may not reach. Repeatable
- `--allow-in <CIDR>`: A source that may reach the sandbox. Repeatable
- `--allow-out-domain <NAME>`: A name the sandbox may reach over HTTP and HTTPS. `*.example.com` covers every name below it, not `example.com`. Repeatable
- `--deny-out-domain <NAME>`: A name the sandbox may not reach, in the same form. Deny beats allow. Repeatable
- `--network <FILE>`: The whole policy as a JSON file, or `-` for stdin: `{"allow_out": [...], "deny_out": [...], "allow_in": [...]}`
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails
